title: Being featured on King Cotton and Pine Top boogie
summary: He was introduced as Larry King Cotton in Washington, and remembers an uncle playing Pine Top.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: The only time I had to play, the only time I had to play, when they featured me on that song I made, King Cotton. I didn't know I was even going to, they said, Cotton, you might be on the program. I said, okay, so we were somewhere. Washington, D.C. And this guy came up there and said, now ladies and gentlemen, we're now going to, here comes Larry King Cotton. I'm looking around to see who is there. I said, oh, that's, I said, man, that's the first time out of the hood Larry before, you know. My name is Lawrence, man. What do you always call Lawrence? Lawrence. Lawrence. Okay. You know, he called me, Larry, what do you mean, Larry? I'm looking around. I'm looking for Larry. I'm looking for Larry. And he said, Larry King Cotton, the spotlight fell on me. And I said, oh yeah. Then I, hit it Cotton, hit it, hit it Cotton. And I went into my little thing, you know, and in a crowd, he went, just play one song, you know, King Cotton, man. And I got into the rhythm of it and everybody, that's the only time I ever played like that. Then I had an uncle who used to play that pine top boogie woogie, man. That was a big song. Man, I wish I had a recording of that so I could play it like he did.
Doctor, I'll find you one. You've got a cassette player? Yeah. I'll put it on cassette for you. We've got some place up here. Somewhere we've got pine top boogie woogie woogie.

Yeah, that's really good, man. He used to play it, man. Man, I used to sit down and just look at him. Because Tommy Darcy, he recorded with the big man. But it's not like when you play it on the piano. Yeah, on the piano, man. My uncle used to play the devil out that thing, man. Yeah.
